assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editing converts a C-G pair to T-A (and A-T to G-C) by deaminase chemistry on DNA without a double-strand break. It is a clear chemical mechanism turned into a general tool for biologists, and it is now moving into patients, which matches what I value most: biology reduced to a defined reaction.
assessment.attribution: Liu's laboratory made the decisive cytosine and adenine base editors; Komor and Gaudelli were lead authors, and Nishida/Kondo's Target-AID is a parallel but secondary route. A single-laureate prize for Liu is cleanest, and I would not stretch to a trio only because the list supplies one.
assessment.maturity: Independently reproduced in many labs and organisms, with early clinical use. Mature enough, and the tool is stable. The CRISPR prize in 2020 makes the timing a judgement call.
uncertainties: Whether the committee sees this as chemistry or as a follow-on to the 2020 CRISPR prize.
Allocation of credit between Liu, his trainees and the independent Target-AID work.
Off-target deamination and bystander editing are still being quantified; I am relying on general knowledge, not checked data.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Hijacking E3 ligases to degrade chosen proteins is a new chemical modality, and the cereblon mechanism for thalidomide and the imides ties an old drug to a defined molecular event. It reshapes drug discovery and is also a tool for acute protein depletion.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies founded the PROTAC concept; Handa identified cereblon as the thalidomide target. Ciulli, Gray and others made major later contributions, so credit is crowded and the three-person split is contestable.
assessment.maturity: Several degraders are in late-stage clinical trials and the mechanism is reproduced widely, but approval of a degrader is still pending, so recognition could be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Who is decisive among the many credited, including Ito, Ciulli and Gray.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Sequencing by synthesis with reversible terminator nucleotides rests on nucleotide chemistry and made genomes cheap to read, with enormous consequences for biology and medicine. Its chemistry is concrete: a blocked, labelled dNTP incorporated by a polymerase and then cleaved.
assessment.attribution: Balasubramanian and Klenerman developed the Solexa chemistry and single-molecule approach; Mayer (clustering), Rothberg (pyrosequencing) and Ju contributed other platforms, so attribution is the main difficulty.
assessment.maturity: The technology is stable, validated and used everywhere. Recognition is overdue rather than premature.
uncertainties: Several competing platforms make a clean, fair split hard.
Whether Sanger-era recognition makes the committee reluctant to honour sequencing again.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Reading single nucleic-acid strands electrically through a pore, with engineered protein pores and a motor enzyme, is chemically and physically elegant and now yields long-read sequencing of DNA, RNA and modifications. It provides the direct measurement I look for.
assessment.attribution: Deamer, Branton and Kasianowicz proposed and showed the principle; Akeson showed base discrimination with polymerase control and Bayley engineered the pores. Branton and Kasianowicz make the credit crowded.
assessment.maturity: Commercial and widely reproduced, but accuracy and some applications were still improving, and the field is still developing.
uncertainties: Priority among Deamer, Branton, Kasianowicz and Akeson is disputed.
Whether this is chemistry or biophysics.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Orthogonal tRNA/synthetase pairs add non-canonical amino acids at chosen codons and so extend protein chemistry inside living cells. It is a general tool and a clear case of making a biological process a defined chemical reaction.
assessment.attribution: Schultz and Wang made the first eukaryotic-compatible and E. coli systems; Chin extended to eukaryotes and recoded genomes; Mehl and Yokoyama are secondary. The trio is plausible.
assessment.maturity: Widely reproduced for two decades and used in therapeutics and imaging, so it is mature. Gains since the first reports have been incremental.
uncertainties: Fair split of credit among the early groups.
Impact on mainstream biochemistry versus niche use.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantitative, large-scale protein mass spectrometry made proteome-wide measurement routine, which matters to me as a measurement-driven biochemist, since dNTP and protein levels are best known by measuring them.
assessment.attribution: Mann, Aebersold and Yates are the usual core trio; Hunt, Gygi and Heck are also credited, so six names compete for three places.
assessment.maturity: A mature and independently validated field. Part of mass spectrometry was recognised in 2002, which reduces the novelty argument.
uncertainties: Six credited names with no obvious natural cut.
Overlap with the 2002 mass spectrometry prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: In vitro selection (SELEX) of functional nucleic acids made aptamers and directed RNA evolution possible and links nucleotide chemistry to function. It has laid groundwork for ribozyme and origin-of-life studies as well as diagnostics and therapeutics.
assessment.attribution: Gold/Tuerk and Ellington/Szostak independently introduced the selection method, and Joyce led evolution of catalytic RNA, so four or five claims compete.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with approved aptamer drugs, though few high-impact uses and a Nobel for directed evolution (2018) already exists.
uncertainties: Credit among Gold, Tuerk, Ellington, Szostak and Joyce.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Covalent targeting of KRAS G12C, via a cysteine-directed ligand and the switch-II pocket, drugged what was long called undruggable. The chemistry is concrete and it led to approved medicines, plus Shokat's chemical genetics of kinases (analog-sensitive alleles).
assessment.attribution: The work is attributable to a single investigator, which gives a clean allocation; later clinical development by companies is not part of the discovery credit.
assessment.maturity: Clinical approval gives strong confirmation, but resistance is limiting durable response and the field is still evolving.
uncertainties: Whether the committee wants a medicinal-chemistry prize this year.
Resistance may change how lasting the impact looks.
